extracted.intended_audience: local officials, community map repository managers, property owners, and any person or entity wishing to inspect, comment on, or appeal FEMA flood hazard determinations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive instructions for inspecting Preliminary and effective FIRMs/FIS reports, submitting comments or appeals on FEMA flood hazard determinations, and for communities to meet NFIP floodplain-management obligations. Covers deadlines, submission addresses, appeal-data requirements, SRP use, and where documents are available for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of flood hazard determination information for inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised flood hazard information for each community is available for inspection at both the online location and the respective community map repository address listed in the table below. Additionally, the current effective FIRM and FIS report for each community are accessible online through the FEMA Map Service Center at https://msc.fema.gov for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary FIRM and, where applicable, FIS reports available at https://hazards.fema.gov/femaportal/prelimdownload; individual community repository addresses are listed in the notice. Interested lessees and owners of real property are encouraged to review the final or preliminary flood hazard information at the cited addresses or online through the FEMA Map Service Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline (proposed determinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are to be submitted on or before August 20, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments identified by Docket No. FEMA—B-2524 to Rick Sacbibit, Chief, Engineering Services Branch, Risk Analysis, Planning & Information Directorate, FEMA, 400 C Street SW, Washington, DC 20472, (202) 646-7659, or (email) patrick.sacbibit@fema.dhs.gov. Preliminary FIRM and FIS are available online for reference when preparing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (docket identification and contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be identified by the applicable Docket No. and submitted to the FEMA contact provided in the notice (Rick Sacbibit) by mail, phone, or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Docket No. (e.g., FEMA—B-2524) when submitting. The notice provides the mailing address, phone number, and email of the responsible official; include relevant map/project identifiers from the tables to ensure comments apply to the correct community/study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration period for finalized determinations (LOMRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the date of the second publication of notification of these changes in a newspaper of local circulation, any person has 90 days in which to request through the community that the Deputy Associate Administrator for Insurance and Mitigation reconsider the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the 90-day period the flood hazard determination information may be changed. Submit requests for reconsideration through the Chief Executive Officer of the community as listed in the notice's table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal criteria for Preliminary FIRM (data requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the revised flood hazard information shown on the Preliminary FIRM and FIS report that satisfies the data requirements outlined in 44 CFR 67.6(b) is considered an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that include the data specified in 44 CFR 67.6(b) should be submitted as appeals; such appeals are considered before the FIRM and FIS report become effective. Comments unrelated to the flood hazard determinations also will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and prerequisites for a Scientific Resolution Panel (SRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a Scientific Resolution Panel (SRP) is available to communities in support of the appeal resolution process. SRPs are independent panels of experts in hydrology, hydraulics, and other pertinent sciences established to review conflicting scientific and technical data and provide recommendations for resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRP may be exercised only after FEMA and local communities have been engaged in a collaborative consultation process for at least 60 days without a mutually acceptable resolution of an appeal. Additional information about the SRP process is available at https://www.floodsrp.org/pdfs/srp_overview.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communities' NFIP floodplain-management obligations (44 CFR 60.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FIRM and FIS report are the basis of the floodplain management measures that the community is required either to adopt or to show evidence of having in effect in order to qualify or remain qualified for participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These flood hazard determinations, together with the floodplain management criteria required by 44 CFR 60.3, are the minimum that are required. They should not be construed to mean that the community must change any existing ordinances that are more stringent; communities may enact stricter requirements at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/regulatory basis and conformity (statutory authority and CFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flood hazard determinations, LOMRs, and proposed determinations are made pursuant to statutory authority (e.g., section 110, 201, or 206 of the Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973; National Flood Insurance Act of 1968) and in accordance with 44 CFR parts 60, 65, and 67 as cited in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to the specific statutory and regulatory provisions establish the legal framework for the determinations, appeals, and required community measures; practitioners should consult the cited U.S. Code sections and 44 CFR provisions for detailed procedural and substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of comments unrelated to flood hazard determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments unrelated to the flood hazard determinations also will be considered before the FIRM and FIS report become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While appeals that meet the data requirements of 44 CFR 67.6(b) are treated as formal appeals, FEMA states it will still consider other substantive comments during the pre-effectiveness period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalization timing and use of effective community number
rubrics_metrics.description: Each LOMR revises the FIRMs (and sometimes the FIS reports) currently in effect for the listed communities. The current effective community number is shown and must be used for all new policies and renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LOMRs are finalized as listed in the notice's table; notice published in local newspapers and 90 days have elapsed since that publication before finalization. Interested parties should use the effective community number shown in the table for insurance transactions.
